method: Fallback image-search descriptions identify familiar classroom use cases. Primary Plimoth Patuxet and Mayflower Society education sources inform clothing, housing, play, food and vessel structure; no source pixels reused.
observations: Common image examples use black outfits and oversized metal hat and shoe buckles; museum sources explain that everyday early-1620s English clothing used varied colors and latchet shoes.
Museum education describes one-room timber homes, domestic work, gardening and learning at home. Games are plausible period examples, not documented portraits of named people.
The museum's reproduction sailing vessel includes principal fore/main/mizzen rigs plus a sprit rig. Do not label an invented vessel a verified exact Mayflower reconstruction.
designDecisions: 44 distinct color compositions and 6 independently arranged coloring outlines, mixing daily activities, clothing, household objects, housing, crafts and voyage scenes.
Use unnamed fictional historical figures and plain colored wool/linen clothing; no named-person identity claims, metal costume buckles, modern appliances or readable invented documents.
Focus this topic on early English colonist life; do not substitute generalized Indigenous costume imagery or claim that these illustrations document the complete history of Thanksgiving.
Review structural supports, tool contacts, hands, historical materials and framing before export.
